assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged kinase targets in oncology, with 7 approved drugs, over 5,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 85 high-resolution crystal structures including ligand-bound complexes at sub-angstrom resolution. The target is primarily implicated in BCR-ABL1-driven chronic myeloid leukemia and is supported by a vast and active literature base of over 1,200 publications. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT is relatively low (63.4) and high-confidence fraction is only 46.3%, likely reflecting disordered regulatory regions (e.g., SH3/SH2 linkers, N-terminal cap) rather than the kinase domain itself — this does not impair druggability assessment given the wealth of experimental structures
Resistance mutations (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) remain a clinical challenge; coverage of all clinically relevant mutant structures may be incomplete
Selectivity profiling across the full kinome for newer inhibitors may be incomplete in ChEMBL
Non-oncology indications (e.g., fibrosis, neurodegeneration) are less well validated despite emerging interest
